page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 2 physical cores, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 2500 GB of NVMe SSD. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression at 34.74 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.0 GB/sec demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weaker; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4390.57 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression of 28.2 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25%. Memory read-only bandwidth is also weak, measuring 340.53 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 34.18 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe storage and DDR5 memory relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a resource-dense option for storage-heavy workloads without needing to scale to larger instance sizes. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. This server is best suited for workloads requiring high local storage capacity and strong single-core execution, such as database operations, text processing, and lightweight web serving.
